title: HTTP/3 RFC 9114 Large Body Completion Verification
verification_method: Focused HTTP/3 loopback tests, QUIC public EOF guardrail tests, touched SpecTrace JSON validation, diff hygiene, and package-backed ProtocolLab H3 proof for the selectable large-body download cells.
scope: This verification covers large HTTP/3 response and upload body completion over the managed Incursa QUIC transport. It does not verify raw QUIC multiplex/duplex throughput or external benchmark publication readiness.
preconditions: The benchmark harness must continue reporting failures and invalid rows honestly.
Content-Length accounting must not be treated as a substitute for correct stream-tail behavior.
procedure: Run focused requirement-home tests for `REQ-QUIC-RFC9114-S4-0002`, `REQ-QUIC-RFC9114-S8-0001`, `REQ-QUIC-RFC9114-S9-0001`, `REQ-QUIC-RFC9114-S9-0002`, and `REQ-QUIC-API-0010`.
Validate the touched SpecTrace JSON artifacts directly when the broader core profile is blocked by unrelated RFC9250 debt.

If the local package inventory can select the H3 large-body cells, run a package-backed ProtocolLab proof for `http.payload.bytes.64kb`, `http.payload.bytes.1mb`, and one upload row with counters enabled.
expected_result: Repeated 64KB and 1MB HTTP/3 responses complete with exact Content-Length, exact DATA frame payload accounting, and stream completion; a response with exact Content-Length bytes but no stream FIN remains incomplete; a response whose DATA bytes are shorter than Content-Length still fails at stream FIN; large uploads deliver exact bodies to handlers; malformed or incomplete framing still fails closed; touched SpecTrace JSON validates; and any ProtocolLab proof is reported only as lab evidence.
status_summary: Focused repo verification covers repeated 64KB and 1MB HTTP/3 responses with exact Content-Length, DATA accounting, and stream completion, the 1MB upload delivery path, incomplete request Content-Length rejection, response Content-Length short-body rejection after stream FIN, the delayed response-FIN client regression that prevents early completion on Content-Length alone, and the REQ-QUIC-API-0010 EOF guardrails. On 2026-06-10, package-backed H3 ProtocolLab proof `job-787e73e89e8b4f6c996909dec53e5568` completed on `plab-worker-sut-01` for suite `h3-large-body-v1`, implementation `quic-dotnet-dev`, test executor `managed-httpclient-h3-load`, and scenarios `http.payload.bytes.64kb` and `http.payload.bytes.1mb`; both cells reported `validation=Passed` and `benchmark=succeeded`. The implementation package was `quic-dotnet-dev:dev-20260611T034152Z-7f4f817f-dirty:84fb2903f22d2f221e50c0c0c8a421456dbc364076874bd3348b43a23d51681e`, with component packages `protocol-lab-managed-h3-test-executor:dev-20260611T034152Z-7f4f817f-dirty:8c4d0fec3630ba15252891ef58792a299833e88ac7933f2eb6822d7b7332ab1a` and `protocol-lab-h3-large-body-scenarios:dev-20260611T034152Z-7f4f817f-dirty:a0470d387d7c87ae3cb7eb6267983a7c700732bd45554250af8743c226cb940f`. The run root is `/opt/protocol-lab/apps/linux-x64/worker/.artifacts/runs/rack-lab-h3-large-body-v1`. This is package-backed lab evidence, not a public benchmark claim.
